notes: WebSearch gave out after six queries (the session's search budget was spent), so the rest was reached directly with the kit's User-Agent (robots.txt asked first): the campaign websites filed with the Secretary of State, county, city and school district sites, the Minnesota DFL's endorsed list and the University of Minnesota's election archive. The 15 candidates of this part's 30 who are not listed below are ones for whom no such page stated anything a card may show.

Not read: co.hubbard.mn.us (robots.txt); genedornink.com (its certificate chain failed and was not bypassed), so no website is recorded for Gene Dornink, a sitting senator; mplsgop.com (timed out), so Abigail Wolters' endorsement is recorded only in her own words and not as endorsed_by; bemidji.k12.mn.us (TLS handshake failed); cityoframsey.com and ci.ramsey.mn.us (TLS name error); the Mahnomen County, Waconia, Big Lake, Mora and New Prague pages show their members only by script; mncourts.gov was not requested (earlier parts found it answers 403), so nothing is recorded for the two judges.
No Republican Party page listing 2026 endorsements was found (mngop.org shows none on its front page), so Patti Mikulski and Gene Dornink have no endorsed_by.

Abigail Wolters' birth year comes from the University of Minnesota Libraries' Minnesota Historical Election Archive, labelled secondary: it is an academic compilation, neither Wikipedia nor a news organization, and it cites the Minnesota Birth Certificate Index. Whether that source is acceptable is for the verifier and John. Only the year is recorded.
Seen and left out: jobs, schools, family and birthplace on campaign sites; the non-party endorsements Jason Heaser's site lists.

Verifier, 2026-10-02: every url was re-opened with the kit's User-Agent and each of the 30 findings was read on its page; each candidate is in part 47 and the office or place on the page matches our record. The Minnesota Historical Election Archive is a university compilation, not Wikipedia or a news organization; it is kept as secondary with its name in the source and the birth date cut to the year. John should say whether that kind of source is acceptable for a birth year.
